recent_commits.body:
REPRODUCED at 2.4.138 on 10.1016/j.joep.2020.102350, Camelot enabled, verified against the RASTERIZED PAGE rather than against another parser. Found by articlerepository-c0 in a 2.4.126 render-baseline; the load-bearing question -- "does CURRENT docpluck still do this?" -- was filed COULD-NOT-VERIFY. It does. rendered bytes 59703 · NUL count 22 CONTROL, same code path, 10.5465/annals.2016.0011 : NUL count 0 p2 Table 1 prints Cramer's V = 0.067 [-0.108, 0.218] <- SPANS zero docpluck emits [ 0.108, 0.218] <- reads as EXCLUDING zero p4 Table 2 "Comparison of differences across conditions" prints Tversky & Shafir, 1992 (between-subjects) 199 -1 -31 -30 213 14 31 17 docpluck emits the three SIGNED values as 1 / 31 / 30 and the three unsigned values intact. The row carries its own two-sided control. All 22 NULs were checked against the page; every one sits where the paper prints a minus. pdftotext recovers the glyph as U+2212, and docpluck's own BODY-TEXT channel gets it right -- the same document renders "[- 0.108," in prose and "[ 0.108," in the table. One document, two channels, two different published values. ROOT CAUSE -- THE REPAIR EXISTS AND CANNOT FIRE. cell_cleaning.py:113-118 already carries it, and its comment names this exact case ('"(cid:0) 31" is -31'): _html_escape("(cid:0) 31") -> "-31" works _html_escape("\x00 31") -> "\x00 31" does nothing Asked of Camelot directly (page 4, flavor=stream): 21 raw cells carry a NUL and NONE carries "(cid:0)". Camelot emits the raw NUL on this path. The older pdfminer-based spike baseline DID emit "(cid:0)", which is presumably why the repair was written that way and why it has looked correct ever since. It is a repair aimed at a representation that no longer arrives. PINNED, NOT FIXED. Five strict xfails; two controls pass. strict=True means a fix turns them XPASS, which pytest reports as a FAILURE -- so the defect cannot be fixed without updating this file. A record of a known defect, not a weakened gate. Not fixed in this commit for one reason, and it is not scope: a fix CHANGES SIGNS in the table channel, a full Camelot suite was already running on a frozen tree, and there is an 08:00 convergence stop. Landing a sign-changing edit that cannot be verified by a full run is the "a fix can be worse than the defect" shape. THE TRAP THE FIX MUST CLEAR, measured and pinned by the last test here: \x00 is ALSO docpluck's own fold sentinel (_MERGE_SEPARATOR = "\x00BR\x00"). A folded header can put a DIGIT right after the closing NUL -- _html_escape("Replication\x00BR\x0095% CI") -> "Replication
95% CI" -- so a naive \x00-before-digit repair inside _html_escape would destroy the fold AND inject a minus that was never printed, turning a data-loss defect into a data-fabrication one. Repair where the Camelot cell is FIRST READ, before any sentinel exists. NOT ESTABLISHED: prevalence (one paper, 22 sites -- proves the shape, not the rate); which versions are affected (2.4.126 and 2.4.138 both reproduce, everything between is presumed affected and unmeasured); whether U+FFFD reaches the same slot. Full diagnosis: docs/FINDINGS_2026-09-02_table_channel_destroys_minus_signs.md

recent_commits.message: Fix Dryad zip-peek auth, multi-sheet Excel detection, and code-in-zip discovery
recent_commits.body:
Four issues found and fixed while validating metacheck against Cooper et
al.'s BES-corpus coding:

- #378/#380: zip_peek() and .remote_size()/.remote_content_length() made
  unauthenticated requests, which Dryad 401s on for any byte-touching
  endpoint. Both now route through the existing .auth_for_url() dispatcher
  instead of requiring each caller to opt in per host.

- #379: data_check's tabular-usability check only ever read the first
  sheet of a multi-sheet Excel workbook. When sheet 1 is a cover/metadata
  page (a common convention), a later sheet holding real tabular data was
  never inspected. data_read_head() now accepts a sheet argument, and
  data_check tries each remaining sheet before giving up on the file.

- #383: code_check() could not see code files inside a zip in three
  compounding ways -- it never read data_check's already-expanded
  structure, it had no zip-peek of its own, and the zip-expansion helper
  (.archive_rows()) discarded code-typed files outright. All three are
  fixed: code_check() prefers data_check's structure when available, gets
  its own zip-peek fallback (.code_expand_zip()), and .archive_rows() now
  keeps code alongside data/documentation.

Also carries the archive_url/archive_member wiring repo_check's zip-peek
expansion always intended (see its own prior comment) so a discovered
member's bytes, not just its name, can be fetched via a byte-range
request against the parent archive -- verified working in every isolated
test, but not yet confirmed reliable end-to-end in the full pipeline
(see #384).

Also fixes data_check's "no readable tabular data" early return silently
omitting structure/previews/gated_repos/manifest_path/group_no_evidence
from its result, which the above fixes depend on being present.

Closes #378, #379, #380, #383

REPRODUCED at 2.4.138 on 10.1016/j.joep.2020.102350, Camelot enabled, verified against the RASTERIZED PAGE rather than against another parser. Found by articlerepository-c0 in a 2.4.126 render-baseline; the load-bearing question -- "does CURRENT docpluck still do this?" -- was filed COULD-NOT-VERIFY. It does. rendered bytes 59703 · NUL count 22 CONTROL, same code path, 10.5465/annals.2016.0011 : NUL count 0 p2 Table 1 prints Cramer's V = 0.067 [-0.108, 0.218] <- SPANS zero docpluck emits [ 0.108, 0.218] <- reads as EXCLUDING zero p4 Table 2 "Comparison of differences across conditions" prints Tversky & Shafir, 1992 (between-subjects) 199 -1 -31 -30 213 14 31 17 docpluck emits the three SIGNED values as 1 / 31 / 30 and the three unsigned values intact. The row carries its own two-sided control. All 22 NULs were checked against the page; every one sits where the paper prints a minus. pdftotext recovers the glyph as U+2212, and docpluck's own BODY-TEXT channel gets it right -- the same document renders "[- 0.108," in prose and "[ 0.108," in the table. One document, two channels, two different published values. ROOT CAUSE -- THE REPAIR EXISTS AND CANNOT FIRE. cell_cleaning.py:113-118 already carries it, and its comment names this exact case ('"(cid:0) 31" is -31'): _html_escape("(cid:0) 31") -> "-31" works _html_escape("\x00 31") -> "\x00 31" does nothing Asked of Camelot directly (page 4, flavor=stream): 21 raw cells carry a NUL and NONE carries "(cid:0)". Camelot emits the raw NUL on this path. The older pdfminer-based spike baseline DID emit "(cid:0)", which is presumably why the repair was written that way and why it has looked correct ever since. It is a repair aimed at a representation that no longer arrives. PINNED, NOT FIXED. Five strict xfails; two controls pass. strict=True means a fix turns them XPASS, which pytest reports as a FAILURE -- so the defect cannot be fixed without updating this file. A record of a known defect, not a weakened gate. Not fixed in this commit for one reason, and it is not scope: a fix CHANGES SIGNS in the table channel, a full Camelot suite was already running on a frozen tree, and there is an 08:00 convergence stop. Landing a sign-changing edit that cannot be verified by a full run is the "a fix can be worse than the defect" shape. THE TRAP THE FIX MUST CLEAR, measured and pinned by the last test here: \x00 is ALSO docpluck's own fold sentinel (_MERGE_SEPARATOR = "\x00BR\x00"). A folded header can put a DIGIT right after the closing NUL -- _html_escape("Replication\x00BR\x0095% CI") -> "Replication
95% CI" -- so a naive \x00-before-digit repair inside _html_escape would destroy the fold AND inject a minus that was never printed, turning a data-loss defect into a data-fabrication one. Repair where the Camelot cell is FIRST READ, before any sentinel exists. NOT ESTABLISHED: prevalence (one paper, 22 sites -- proves the shape, not the rate); which versions are affected (2.4.126 and 2.4.138 both reproduce, everything between is presumed affected and unmeasured); whether U+FFFD reaches the same slot. Full diagnosis: docs/FINDINGS_2026-09-02_table_channel_destroys_minus_signs.md

recent_commits.message: tools+tests: 16 harness scripts imported the INSTALLED release, not the tree
recent_commits.body:
Python puts THE SCRIPT'S OWN DIRECTORY on sys.path[0], never the cwd, so a
script under tools/ or scripts/ has no route to the repo root and a bare
`import docpluck` silently resolves to whatever is installed.

Measured 2026-09-01 on this tree, three arms:

    python tools/<probe>.py         -> site-packages\docpluck  2.4.137
    python -c "import docpluck"     -> <repo>\docpluck         2.4.138
    python <probe-at-repo-root>.py  -> <repo>\docpluck         2.4.138

The third arm is the control: it isolates the cause to the script's DIRECTORY
rather than to "running a script at all". Arm two is structurally incapable of
showing the defect, which is why it survived -- the obvious check measures a
different thing.

Census of all 34 docpluck importers under tools/ + scripts/: 16 resolved the
installed 2.4.137, INCLUDING scripts/verify_corpus.py, the 26-paper baseline
that gates every iterate cycle. A fix could be verified all night against a
library it had not touched, with every log line naming the tree.

This generalises W-0011 (52903fe), which repaired ONE script -- render_for_audit

recent_commits.message: tests: pin the table channel destroying minus signs (repair cannot fire)
recent_commits.body:
REPRODUCED at 2.4.138 on 10.1016/j.joep.2020.102350, Camelot enabled, verified against the RASTERIZED PAGE rather than against another parser. Found by articlerepository-c0 in a 2.4.126 render-baseline; the load-bearing question -- "does CURRENT docpluck still do this?" -- was filed COULD-NOT-VERIFY. It does. rendered bytes 59703 · NUL count 22 CONTROL, same code path, 10.5465/annals.2016.0011 : NUL count 0 p2 Table 1 prints Cramer's V = 0.067 [-0.108, 0.218] <- SPANS zero docpluck emits [ 0.108, 0.218] <- reads as EXCLUDING zero p4 Table 2 "Comparison of differences across conditions" prints Tversky & Shafir, 1992 (between-subjects) 199 -1 -31 -30 213 14 31 17 docpluck emits the three SIGNED values as 1 / 31 / 30 and the three unsigned values intact. The row carries its own two-sided control. All 22 NULs were checked against the page; every one sits where the paper prints a minus. pdftotext recovers the glyph as U+2212, and docpluck's own BODY-TEXT channel gets it right -- the same document renders "[- 0.108," in prose and "[ 0.108," in the table. One document, two channels, two different published values. ROOT CAUSE -- THE REPAIR EXISTS AND CANNOT FIRE. cell_cleaning.py:113-118 already carries it, and its comment names this exact case ('"(cid:0) 31" is -31'): _html_escape("(cid:0) 31") -> "-31" works _html_escape("\x00 31") -> "\x00 31" does nothing Asked of Camelot directly (page 4, flavor=stream): 21 raw cells carry a NUL and NONE carries "(cid:0)". Camelot emits the raw NUL on this path. The older pdfminer-based spike baseline DID emit "(cid:0)", which is presumably why the repair was written that way and why it has looked correct ever since. It is a repair aimed at a representation that no longer arrives. PINNED, NOT FIXED. Five strict xfails; two controls pass. strict=True means a fix turns them XPASS, which pytest reports as a FAILURE -- so the defect cannot be fixed without updating this file. A record of a known defect, not a weakened gate. Not fixed in this commit for one reason, and it is not scope: a fix CHANGES SIGNS in the table channel, a full Camelot suite was already running on a frozen tree, and there is an 08:00 convergence stop. Landing a sign-changing edit that cannot be verified by a full run is the "a fix can be worse than the defect" shape. THE TRAP THE FIX MUST CLEAR, measured and pinned by the last test here: \x00 is ALSO docpluck's own fold sentinel (_MERGE_SEPARATOR = "\x00BR\x00"). A folded header can put a DIGIT right after the closing NUL -- _html_escape("Replication\x00BR\x0095% CI") -> "Replication
95% CI" -- so a naive \x00-before-digit repair inside _html_escape would destroy the fold AND inject a minus that was never printed, turning a data-loss defect into a data-fabrication one. Repair where the Camelot cell is FIRST READ, before any sentinel exists. NOT ESTABLISHED: prevalence (one paper, 22 sites -- proves the shape, not the rate); which versions are affected (2.4.126 and 2.4.138 both reproduce, everything between is presumed affected and unmeasured); whether U+FFFD reaches the same slot. Full diagnosis: docs/FINDINGS_2026-09-02_table_channel_destroys_minus_signs.md

REPRODUCED at 2.4.138 on 10.1016/j.joep.2020.102350, Camelot enabled, verified against the RASTERIZED PAGE rather than against another parser. Found by articlerepository-c0 in a 2.4.126 render-baseline; the load-bearing question -- "does CURRENT docpluck still do this?" -- was filed COULD-NOT-VERIFY. It does. rendered bytes 59703 · NUL count 22 CONTROL, same code path, 10.5465/annals.2016.0011 : NUL count 0 p2 Table 1 prints Cramer's V = 0.067 [-0.108, 0.218] <- SPANS zero docpluck emits [ 0.108, 0.218] <- reads as EXCLUDING zero p4 Table 2 "Comparison of differences across conditions" prints Tversky & Shafir, 1992 (between-subjects) 199 -1 -31 -30 213 14 31 17 docpluck emits the three SIGNED values as 1 / 31 / 30 and the three unsigned values intact. The row carries its own two-sided control. All 22 NULs were checked against the page; every one sits where the paper prints a minus. pdftotext recovers the glyph as U+2212, and docpluck's own BODY-TEXT channel gets it right -- the same document renders "[- 0.108," in prose and "[ 0.108," in the table. One document, two channels, two different published values. ROOT CAUSE -- THE REPAIR EXISTS AND CANNOT FIRE. cell_cleaning.py:113-118 already carries it, and its comment names this exact case ('"(cid:0) 31" is -31'): _html_escape("(cid:0) 31") -> "-31" works _html_escape("\x00 31") -> "\x00 31" does nothing Asked of Camelot directly (page 4, flavor=stream): 21 raw cells carry a NUL and NONE carries "(cid:0)". Camelot emits the raw NUL on this path. The older pdfminer-based spike baseline DID emit "(cid:0)", which is presumably why the repair was written that way and why it has looked correct ever since. It is a repair aimed at a representation that no longer arrives. PINNED, NOT FIXED. Five strict xfails; two controls pass. strict=True means a fix turns them XPASS, which pytest reports as a FAILURE -- so the defect cannot be fixed without updating this file. A record of a known defect, not a weakened gate. Not fixed in this commit for one reason, and it is not scope: a fix CHANGES SIGNS in the table channel, a full Camelot suite was already running on a frozen tree, and there is an 08:00 convergence stop. Landing a sign-changing edit that cannot be verified by a full run is the "a fix can be worse than the defect" shape. THE TRAP THE FIX MUST CLEAR, measured and pinned by the last test here: \x00 is ALSO docpluck's own fold sentinel (_MERGE_SEPARATOR = "\x00BR\x00"). A folded header can put a DIGIT right after the closing NUL -- _html_escape("Replication\x00BR\x0095% CI") -> "Replication
95% CI" -- so a naive \x00-before-digit repair inside _html_escape would destroy the fold AND inject a minus that was never printed, turning a data-loss defect into a data-fabrication one. Repair where the Camelot cell is FIRST READ, before any sentinel exists. NOT ESTABLISHED: prevalence (one paper, 22 sites -- proves the shape, not the rate); which versions are affected (2.4.126 and 2.4.138 both reproduce, everything between is presumed affected and unmeasured); whether U+FFFD reaches the same slot. recent_commits.body:
Python puts THE SCRIPT'S OWN DIRECTORY on sys.path[0], never the cwd, so a
script under tools/ or scripts/ has no route to the repo root and a bare
`import docpluck` silently resolves to whatever is installed.

Measured 2026-09-01 on this tree, three arms:

    python tools/<probe>.py         -> site-packages\docpluck  2.4.137
    python -c "import docpluck"     -> <repo>\docpluck         2.4.138
    python <probe-at-repo-root>.py  -> <repo>\docpluck         2.4.138

The third arm is the control: it isolates the cause to the script's DIRECTORY
rather than to "running a script at all". Arm two is structurally incapable of
showing the defect, which is why it survived -- the obvious check measures a
different thing.

Census of all 34 docpluck importers under tools/ + scripts/: 16 resolved the
installed 2.4.137, INCLUDING scripts/verify_corpus.py, the 26-paper baseline
that gates every iterate cycle. A fix could be verified all night against a
library it had not touched, with every log line naming the tree.

This generalises W-0011 (52903fe), which repaired ONE script -- render_for_audit
-- while the same defect sat in fifteen others.

THE FIX is keyed on the pyproject.toml marker rather than a parents[N] count:
tools/*.py needs 1 and tools/diag/*.py needs 2, so a count encodes the file's
current location into its correctness and silently regresses the moment a file
moves -- regresses in the direction that resolves site-packages again.

THE GATE is now a test, not a one-off census: 16 failed -> 35 passed, watched
red first. It runs each script for real under runpy with sys.path[0] set to the
script's own directory and halts at the moment docpluck is imported.

Four earlier probe designs each made correctly-guarded scripts look defective:
`python -c` has no __file__, so every Path(__file__).parents[N] guard raised
NameError; line-slicing the prologue left a multi-line `from docpluck.x import (`
unclosed; extending the block ran on into argparse; an empty argparse Namespace
stub crashed four scripts that read their own options at module level. Each was
caught only because the test scores a failed MEASUREMENT as a failure, never as
a pass -- a skip, an N/A and an indeterminate are all green-shaped and none of
them is a measurement.

NOT INCLUDED, deliberately. Three scripts also carry this fix in the working
tree but are NOT in this commit, because each already held another stream's
uncommitted work and committing them would sign it:
  scripts/verify_corpus.py                       (+ a stdout/stderr reconfigure block)
  tools/diag/form_feed_page_attribution_census.py   (untracked, page-gate stream)
  tools/diag/repeated_line_gate_census.py            (untracked, page-gate stream)
The gate test will therefore report verify_corpus.py red on a fresh checkout.
That is accurate and visible rather than hidden, and the authorship decision is
the owner's.

EVIDENTIARY CONSEQUENCE for anyone citing past measurements: every zero proved
with tools/diag/repair_site_scan.py before this commit describes released
2.4.137, not this repository. Same for any prevalence figure from the two
census scripts named above.

Suite: 3060 passed / 13 failed (was 3024 / 14). All 13 pre-date this change:
the guard is provably inert under pytest (the repo root is already on sys.path,
so the insert is a no-op) and tools/diag/_corpus.py, the only module the failing
tests import from tools/, is untouched and not dirty.

recent_commits.message: fix(batch): a key `get_version_info()` reports and `ExtractionReport` has no field for is a CRASH, not a gap — and the tripwire fired into an empty room
recent_commits.body:
`047b4ca` added `git_state` to `get_version_info()` and did not add the matching
field to `ExtractionReport`. `extract_to_dir()` builds that report by SPLATTING
the version dict into the constructor, so the missing field is not a silent
`"unknown"` — it is:

    TypeError: ExtractionReport.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument
               'git_state'. Did you mean 'git_sha'?

raised at batch.py:282, BEFORE the per-file try/except, so the whole function
dies rather than recording a per-file error.

THE SPLAT IS A DELIBERATE TRIPWIRE AND IT WORKED. Its own docstring predicts
this exact failure — "a key added to `get_version_info()` without a matching
field then raises TypeError on the first batch run, which is loud and
immediate" — and rejects the field-by-field alternative precisely because that
one would ship a receipt that looks complete and is not. The defect was not the
design. It was committing without running the suite: `core.hooksPath` had
pointed at a dead path since 2026-08-03, so no gate ran on `047b4ca` at all.

ELEVEN TEST SIGNALS, ONE ROOT CAUSE — every one an `extract_to_dir` caller:

  5 ERRORS  test_provenance_completeness::TestWrittenReceiptAndSidecar
            (the class fixture calls extract_to_dir and asserts n_ok == 1;
             an assert inside a fixture is an ERROR, not a FAIL — which is
             why five consecutive E's appeared with no failure text)
  2 FAILS   test_provenance_completeness::TestReportProvenance
            (the field-completeness guards — i.e. the check for exactly this)
  2 FAILS   test_metaesci_followups::TestExtractToDir
  2 FAILS   test_batch_scans_for_symbol_font_corruption

LIVE FOR A CONSUMER, not merely pending a tag. MetaESCI runs an EDITABLE
install of this checkout — `find_spec('docpluck').origin` resolves to this
working tree — and `src/03_process/extract_text.py:75` calls `extract_to_dir`
directly with no try/except, so its entire text-extraction stage was crashing
from the moment `047b4ca` landed. `047b4ca` is unpushed and untagged, so PyPI,
the app pin and production were never affected; production serves 1.9.58.

`git_state` is now a field on `ExtractionReport`, with a default because
`git_sha` above it is positional. It reaches `to_dict()`, `write_receipt()` and
the per-file `.json` sidecar — those two were already built from `info`
wholesale, so only the dataclass was missing. A SHA ALONE IS NOT AN IDENTITY:
a receipt reading `git_sha: 047b4ca` for a run against a tree with uncommitted
edits names a commit whose code never ran, which is the whole reason
`git_state` was added and why omitting it from the receipt would have defeated
its purpose.

Verified beyond our own tests, against the downstream consumer's own adapter:
MetaESCI `extract_to_staging` -> n_ok=1, n_failed=0, git_state='dirty'.
The four affected test files: 61 passed, 1 skipped.

NOT INCLUDED, DELIBERATELY: `docpluck/normalize.py` stays uncommitted. A

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): `eta` is not a substring of ordinary English — and the receipt can now name the tree
recent_commits.body:
CHANGES EXTRACTION OUTPUT. Consumer goldens may legitimately move.

`_EFFECT_TYPE_PATTERNS` ended both of its eta alternatives with a bare,
unanchored `eta`, and `_effect_type_for` runs over the whole CAPTION AND
FOOTNOTE. So `Cardiom-eta-bolic`, `b-eta`, `th-eta` and `M-eta-analysis` each
typed EVERY unlabeled estimate column in their table as eta-squared.

Reported by Scimeto/CitationGuard against a JAMA Netw Open table captioned
"... Cardiometabolic Risk Factors": 19 rows emitted with an `eta2` field, 18 of
them OUTSIDE eta-squared's domain [0, 1] (17 negative, one at 10.65), against
ZERO occurrences of any eta token in the extracted text. The column was headed
"mean change from baseline (95% CI)" — kilograms and percent, not variance
proportions.

This is a FABRICATION, not a miss: docpluck naming a statistic the paper does
not report. `beta coefficient` -> partial eta-squared is the same defect
relabelling a different statistic. Every other defect this week DELETES data;
this one INVENTS it.

The domain guard that should have caught it was gated on `eta2_inferred`, which
is true only on the `_infer_anova_eta2_hint` path (requires an F in the row).
When the key came instead from the CAPTION vocabulary — the weakest of the
three evidence sources — the guard was skipped entirely. The docstring promised
"a stray non-proportion estimate is never mistyped"; the promise held only on
the path the guard happened to be attached to. Both are fixed.

AUTHORSHIP: the flatten.py fix and tests/test_eta_is_not_a_substring.py were
authored by an earlier session and were sitting uncommitted in the shared tree.
This session verified rather than wrote them: 9 of 18 assertions RED against
HEAD's flatten.py in an isolated `git archive HEAD` tree, 18 green here.
Committed by this session so the fix stops being unnameable.

---

`git_state` in get_version_info() — because that last sentence is the point.

Most of this portfolio consumes docpluck through `pip install -e`, which
executes whatever is in the working tree while `git rev-parse HEAD` reports the
last commit. Every uncommitted edit therefore shipped under a SHA that does not
contain it.

paths modified, `normalize.py` among them — a file whose changes alter
extraction output. A consumer on the editable install would have been running
that normalization and recording `git_sha: 9504ad9` for it. `dirty` appeared
ZERO times anywhere under `docpluck/`.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): v1.9.59 — a page NUMBER is in the margin; a bare integer in the BODY is a value
recent_commits.body:
The standalone-page-number strip was one MULTILINE substitution with no page
context, so it deleted EVERY line whose whole content was a 1-3 digit integer —
and pdftotext emits a narrow numeric table column as ONE CELL PER LINE. It was
silently selective: -4, 0.5 and 1000 never matched; 0, 4 and 999 always did.

MEASURED on 10.1136/bmj-2024-080924 (BMJ) supplementary appendix Table S1 p6,
row "Number of Advancement Maneuvers (attempt #2)": the paper prints a
coefficient of 0 with (-1.5 to 1.5) and p = 0.999, and we delivered the interval
and the p-value WITH NO ESTIMATE — worse than a wrong number, because an
interval attached to nothing cannot even be attributed. This is the real content
of ESCImate 2026-08-09/DP-14, which both sides had diagnosed as a "column-major
dump"; the source text layer is row-major and complete, and this rule punched
the holes.

The gate is TYPOGRAPHIC: a page number is drawn in the margin, so it must be
among the first or last 2 non-blank lines of its page. A SECOND gate strips a
PAGINATION RUN wherever it sits (value - page_index constant across >=3 distinct
pages), because a two-column PDF puts the number mid-stream in pdftotext reading
order; a table column cannot satisfy that, its integers sit on ONE page.

Corpus effect over the 26-paper baseline, old rule vs new: 1,228 bare-integer
lines RETAINED, 1,104 still stripped, LINE COUNT identical on all 26 papers.

Also in this change:
* NormalizationReport.changes_made now ACCUMULATES instead of overwriting.
  Three rules write dropped_minus_signs_recovered and three write
  minus_signs_recovered, so only the last survived. Filed by ESCImate
  2026-08-21 §4, who had to publish upstream_sign_rewrites as a LOWER BOUND.
* changes_made_by_step records every changed step INCLUDING length-neutral ones
  — a '2' -> '-' glyph substitution has a delta of zero, so the rules this
  metric exists for were the ones most likely to vanish from it.
* v1.9.58 residual_control_chars documentation.

AUTHORSHIP — this work was NOT written by the session committing it. It was
authored across several concurrent docpluck sessions on 2026-08-22 and left
uncommitted in a shared working tree. Committed by an unrelated session on the
repository owner's explicit instruction, to preserve a data-loss fix that
existed nowhere but that tree. Credit belongs to the original authors.

Committed strictly by explicit pathspec. Deliberately NOT included, because they
are separate work streams still owned by their authors: the sectioning_text_id
change (docpluck/sections/*, tests/test_sectioning_text_id.py,
tools/diag/section_confidence_census.py), the `eta`-as-substring table fix
(docpluck/tables/flatten.py, tests/test_eta_is_not_a_substring.py),
scripts/harness/extract.py (unclaimed), and scripts/verify_corpus.py.

docpluck/__init__.py is staged PARTIALLY — the version bump only. Its
sectioning_text_id export belongs to the sectioning stream, and committing it
here would import a symbol that does not exist in this tree.

Verified before committing: the staged tree imports cleanly, reports
2.4.138 / 1.9.59, does not export sectioning_text_id, and 220 tests pass
against it.

No tag, no release, no push.

recent_commits.body:
v1.9.57 diagnosed that one stray U+0008 BACKSPACE made a Frontiers running
header unequal to its layout-channel twin, and fixed it inside `_key()` — F0's
comparison key. The character stayed in the emitted text, where a completely
unrelated rule landed on it one day later:
`_prior_paragraph_is_sentence_terminated` walks back over whitespace and
requires what it finds to be in ".!?/". On 10.3389/fvets.2025.1645266 the walk
landed on the BACKSPACE, discarded the `1 Introduction:` heading, and greedy
span-fill handed the preceding KEYWORDS span 69,849 characters — the whole
article. Found by an external benchmark, not by us.

* C0 `_strip_furniture_controls` (NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.58), run before F0
  so the comparison key and the output are ONE rule. One character wide and
  measured: all 33 corpus U+0008 sites are '.'+BS+newline, none are overstrike.
  U+0002/03/04/07 are corrupted CONTENT glyphs (Schri<02>macher =
  "Schrittmacher") and are COUNTED, not stripped, in the new
  `NormalizationReport.residual_control_chars`.

  heading carrying BOTH a line-initial section number AND a colon no longer
  needs a terminated prior paragraph (SECTIONING_VERSION 1.2.5). Both halves
  are required: `2 Literature search` on the same paper resolves canonically to
  `references`, so a number-only escape would open back-matter mid-article.
  Measured blast radius: 3 of 39 guard rejections were furniture; the escape
  fires exactly once in 30 papers.

  set(SectionLabel)` matched every label), is deleted.

because it stripped the character from an already-normalized string while the
shipped order runs C0 before H0. Test the composition that ships (LESSONS
L-055, L-056).

oracle 0.8038 -> 0.8140, collapses 5 -> 4, recall median 0.9862, 0 regressions.

recent_commits.message: test(gate): the docs-accuracy gate had no test, and was edited twice in one session
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/check_docs_consistency.py` asserts that the version numbers
`docs/README.md` advertises still match the constants this package defines. It is
invoked by hand from handoffs and release checklists and by nothing automatic —
so it was changed twice today (2657047, ab291c7) with nothing pinning either
change, and the second of those changes existed only because the first had a gap
nobody could have caught.

A check that CAN be a test MUST be a test. A gate nobody runs is
indistinguishable from a gate that passes, and this one guards a claim that
reaches consumers: `docs/README.md` documents the provenance block
`get_version_info()` returns.

Five cases, each pinning a failure that actually happened or is about to:

  * the gate PASSES on the committed tree
  * a drifted PACKAGE version is caught — the one that goes stale on EVERY
    release, uncovered until ab291c7
  * a drifted PIPELINE version is caught — `table_extraction_version` sat at
    '2.4.10' against a source 2.4.12 until it was spotted by eye
  * a drifted NORMALIZATION version is caught
  * the two deliberately-ungated keys are still NAMED in the gate, so the reason
    for excluding them cannot be silently lost

Each drift runs against a COPY of only the files the gate reads, in tmp — the
test never mutates the working tree, and does not drag the corpus along.

MUTATION-VERIFIED IN TWO DIRECTIONS, because a test that has never failed against
the real defect proves nothing:

  removing the package-version line   -> exactly 1 test fails
  removing the whole sibling loop     -> 3 tests fail

recent_commits.message: fix(gate): the version check missed the ONE version that goes stale every release
recent_commits.body:
Hard rule 23 says a universal-quantifier claim is only as good as the enumeration
behind it. The previous commit's message claimed the gate "compares every
advertised pipeline version against its defining constant". Enumerating the
provenance block in docs/README.md rather than trusting that sentence:

    advertised   version, normalize_version, sectioning_version,
                 table_extraction_version, python_version, unicodedata_version
    covered      normalize_version, sectioning_version, table_extraction_version
    UNCOVERED    version, python_version, unicodedata_version

Six keys, not the five I had in mind -- `unicodedata_version` was not even on my
list. The claim was defensible for the three PIPELINE versions and silent about
the rest, which is exactly the shape rule 23 exists to catch.

`version` is now covered, and it is the important one: it is the package version,
so it goes stale on EVERY release, and docs/README.md advertises it as `2.4.135`.
The very next release would have made that doc wrong with nothing to say so.

`python_version` and `unicodedata_version` are deliberately NOT gated, and the
code says why: they are runtime facts this repo does not define, so there is no
constant for them to drift from. Recording the reason matters more than the
exclusion -- an unexplained gap reads as an oversight to the next maintainer.

Mutation-verified: setting __version__ = 2.4.136 fails with
"docs/README.md says version = '2.4.135' but docpluck/__init__.py defines
__version__ = '2.4.136'", and restoring it passes.

recent_commits.message: Raise Dryad zip-vs-file threshold from 4 to 12 files
recent_commits.body:
Even at the original threshold of 4, the ZIP BUCKET'S HOURLY CAP
(20/hour -- separate from, and much tighter than, the 100/day ceiling)
was still being tripped repeatedly. Confirmed live against the real
Cooper-validation corpus run: batch 29 hit the same 5-file dataset's
zip request on three consecutive restarts, because restarting the
script does not reset the host's quota clock -- only real elapsed time
does, and not enough had passed between attempts.

Recomputed against the corpus data on disk at the time (873 Dryad
datasets): threshold 4 needs 190 zip requests corpus-wide, a 9.5/hour
average even under the best-case 2-day spread -- already exceeding the
20/hour ceiling on average, before accounting for a real run's uneven,
bursty pacing. Threshold 12 needs only 33 zip requests corpus-wide
(1.6/hour average), a far larger safety margin against the hourly wall
specifically.

This trades away some of the daily-quota-optimality the original
threshold-sweep found (12 is not that sweep's minimum-day threshold,
3-6 was) for practical hourly headroom that matters more once a real
run is actually hitting the hourly cap repeatedly.

Updated the "still uses zip" unit test from 8 to 16 files to stay above
the new threshold. Full file-level test-repo-download.R suite passes
clean (FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 1 | PASS 77).

recent_commits.message: Make Dryad's zip-vs-file-by-file download choice quota-aware
recent_commits.body:
Dryad throttles zip downloads and per-file downloads through two
independent per-IP quota buckets with very different sizes (confirmed
2026-09-01 against Dryad's own open-source rate-limit config,
datadryad/dryad-app config/initializers/rack_attack.rb +
config/app_config.yml): zip_downloads_per_day = 100,
file_downloads_per_day = 500 -- 5x more headroom on the file bucket.

The existing zip-vs-file decision only weighed request-count efficiency
(worth_it <- n_wanted > 50 || record_n <= 2*n_wanted), which picks zip
for nearly every real dataset since callers almost always want "all of
it". That means every Dryad dataset routed through the strict 100/day
zip bucket while the much larger 500/day file bucket sat unused.

Recomputed against the real Cooper-validation corpus (768 Dryad
datasets, 2710 files, 26 completed batches): always-zip needs 8
calendar days minimum (768 requests / 100 per day); always-file needs
6 (2710 / 500); routing small datasets (<=4 files) to the file bucket
and only larger ones to the zip bucket needs 3 -- the minimum across
every threshold from 0-50 tested, because it's the point where both
buckets fill up on the same day instead of one sitting idle while the
other alone is the bottleneck.

Added a `quota_worth_it <- n_wanted > 4L` gate ANDed onto the existing
request-count check, Dryad-only. Not applied to OSF/Zenodo/Dataverse/
GitHub/GitLab's identical-looking worth_it lines elsewhere in the same
file -- only Dryad's independent-stacked-throttle asymmetry has been
confirmed; changing the shared logic for hosts whose rate-limit
behaviour was never verified would be a separate, unjustified change.

Two new unit tests confirm a small Dryad dataset skips zip even though
the old request-count-only logic would have picked it, and a larger
one still uses zip. Full package test suite passes clean
(FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 68 | PASS 4327).

recent_commits.message: release: v2.4.137 — a fix in the COMPARISON KEY is not a fix in the SHIPPED string
recent_commits.body:
v1.9.57 diagnosed that one stray U+0008 BACKSPACE made a Frontiers running
header unequal to its layout-channel twin, and fixed it inside `_key()` — F0's
comparison key. The character stayed in the emitted text, where a completely
unrelated rule landed on it one day later:
`_prior_paragraph_is_sentence_terminated` walks back over whitespace and
requires what it finds to be in ".!?/". On 10.3389/fvets.2025.1645266 the walk
landed on the BACKSPACE, discarded the `1 Introduction:` heading, and greedy
span-fill handed the preceding KEYWORDS span 69,849 characters — the whole
article. Found by an external benchmark, not by us.

* C0 `_strip_furniture_controls` (NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.58), run before F0
  so the comparison key and the output are ONE rule. One character wide and
  measured: all 33 corpus U+0008 sites are '.'+BS+newline, none are overstrike.
  U+0002/03/04/07 are corrupted CONTENT glyphs (Schri<02>macher =
  "Schrittmacher") and are COUNTED, not stripped, in the new
  `NormalizationReport.residual_control_chars`.
* The heading guard skips page breaks and control characters, and a canonical
  heading carrying BOTH a line-initial section number AND a colon no longer
  needs a terminated prior paragraph (SECTIONING_VERSION 1.2.5). Both halves
  are required: `2 Literature search` on the same paper resolves canonically to
  `references`, so a number-only escape would open back-matter mid-article.
  Measured blast radius: 3 of 39 guard rejections were furniture; the escape
  fires exactly once in 30 papers.

  set(SectionLabel)` matched every label), is deleted.

because it stripped the character from an already-normalized string while the
shipped order runs C0 before H0. Test the composition that ships (LESSONS
L-055, L-056).

oracle 0.8038 -> 0.8140, collapses 5 -> 4, recall median 0.9862, 0 regressions.

no indication of which callers see it. Two of those three claims do not reach the
HTTP API at all, and the entry as written told consumers otherwise.

the footnote appendix is F0's product. Enumerated rather than assumed:

    batch.py:355              passes layout   -> full change
    sections/__init__.py:116  passes layout   -> full change
    service/app/main.py:532   NO layout       -> page breaks only
    service/app/main.py:1007  NO layout       -> page breaks only

Re-measured through the no-layout path the service actually runs: 12 of 26 papers
change (not 16), 0 appendices restored (not 2), and still 0 lines removed or
added. The API gains page boundaries and loses nothing; it gains no appendix.

AND THE LARGER FINDING, pre-existing and not this release's doing: because the
service never computes a layout, F0 has NEVER run in production, and neither has
any layout-gated repair -- W0h (dropped minus via cid glyph), W0m (beta-as-b via
font), W0p (superscript via size+baseline). Every API consumer has been receiving
text with running headers intact and those three repairs absent, while the same
document through `extract_to_dir` is repaired. Two paths, one version, different
numbers.

This is the identical shape CLAUDE.md records for batch.py and marks FIXED in
v2.4.128 -- the service was never checked. NOT fixed here: wiring a layout into
the service roughly doubles per-document cost and changes output for every
consumer at once, which is a deliberate decision, not a doc fix. Tracked in the
handoff and in both consumer notices.

recent_commits.message: Raise Dryad zip-vs-file threshold from 4 to 12 files
recent_commits.body:
Even at the original threshold of 4, the ZIP BUCKET'S HOURLY CAP
(20/hour -- separate from, and much tighter than, the 100/day ceiling)
was still being tripped repeatedly. Confirmed live against the real
Cooper-validation corpus run: batch 29 hit the same 5-file dataset's
zip request on three consecutive restarts, because restarting the
script does not reset the host's quota clock -- only real elapsed time
does, and not enough had passed between attempts.

Recomputed against the corpus data on disk at the time (873 Dryad
datasets): threshold 4 needs 190 zip requests corpus-wide, a 9.5/hour
average even under the best-case 2-day spread -- already exceeding the
20/hour ceiling on average, before accounting for a real run's uneven,
bursty pacing. Threshold 12 needs only 33 zip requests corpus-wide
(1.6/hour average), a far larger safety margin against the hourly wall
specifically.

This trades away some of the daily-quota-optimality the original
threshold-sweep found (12 is not that sweep's minimum-day threshold,
3-6 was) for practical hourly headroom that matters more once a real
run is actually hitting the hourly cap repeatedly.

Updated the "still uses zip" unit test from 8 to 16 files to stay above
the new threshold. Full file-level test-repo-download.R suite passes
clean (FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 1 | PASS 77).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Make Dryad's zip-vs-file-by-file download choice quota-aware
recent_commits.body:
Dryad throttles zip downloads and per-file downloads through two
independent per-IP quota buckets with very different sizes (confirmed
2026-09-01 against Dryad's own open-source rate-limit config,
datadryad/dryad-app config/initializers/rack_attack.rb +
config/app_config.yml): zip_downloads_per_day = 100,
file_downloads_per_day = 500 -- 5x more headroom on the file bucket.

The existing zip-vs-file decision only weighed request-count efficiency
(worth_it <- n_wanted > 50 || record_n <= 2*n_wanted), which picks zip
for nearly every real dataset since callers almost always want "all of
it". That means every Dryad dataset routed through the strict 100/day
zip bucket while the much larger 500/day file bucket sat unused.

Recomputed against the real Cooper-validation corpus (768 Dryad
datasets, 2710 files, 26 completed batches): always-zip needs 8
calendar days minimum (768 requests / 100 per day); always-file needs
6 (2710 / 500); routing small datasets (<=4 files) to the file bucket
and only larger ones to the zip bucket needs 3 -- the minimum across
every threshold from 0-50 tested, because it's the point where both
buckets fill up on the same day instead of one sitting idle while the
other alone is the bottleneck.

Added a `quota_worth_it <- n_wanted > 4L` gate ANDed onto the existing
request-count check, Dryad-only. Not applied to OSF/Zenodo/Dataverse/
GitHub/GitLab's identical-looking worth_it lines elsewhere in the same
file -- only Dryad's independent-stacked-throttle asymmetry has been
confirmed; changing the shared logic for hosts whose rate-limit
behaviour was never verified would be a separate, unjustified change.

Two new unit tests confirm a small Dryad dataset skips zip even though
the old request-count-only logic would have picked it, and a larger
one still uses zip. Full package test suite passes clean
(FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 68 | PASS 4327).

recent_commits.message: Fix code_check crash when every file in a batch fails to download
recent_commits.body:
Three related bugs in code_check.R, all triggered by the same real-world
condition: every code file for a paper fails to download (e.g. a Dryad
rate limit genuinely exhausted mid-corpus-run), leaving code_files with
no rows that ever reached the per-file try block, so several columns are
absent entirely rather than NA-filled.

1. `sapply(code_files$library_max_between > 3, isTRUE)` on a zero-length
   input silently returns list() instead of logical(0). Subscripting
   code_files$file_name with that list() throws "invalid subscript type
   'list'" -- this is what actually crashed batch 27 of the Cooper
   validation corpus run. Fixed with vapply(), whose declared FUN.VALUE
   always returns the right type regardless of input length.

2. The comments-table block assumed `percentage_comment` always exists as
   a column and threw "undefined columns selected" when it didn't. Now
   guarded the same way n_analysed/comment_issue already handled it
   (treat an absent column as nothing to report).

3. The final summary_table `dplyr::summarise()` referenced code_abs_path,
   loaded_files_missing, percentage_comment, and parse_error unguarded.
   code_setwd already had an `if (col %in% names(code_files))` guard for
   the same reason; the other four did not. Added the same guard to all
   of them via a small has_col() helper.

Reproduced deterministically with a mocked download_repo_files() that
always fails, added as a regression test. Full package test suite passes
clean (FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 68 | PASS 4323).

recent_commits.body: Wait for the real Dryad/Zenodo/GitHub/GitLab rate-limit reset instead of blind exponential backoff
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Wait for the real rate-limit reset instead of blind exponential backoff
recent_commits.body:
Found while investigating a code_check crash in a real 1861-paper corpus
run: Dryad's file-download endpoint sends IETF-draft RateLimit-Limit/
RateLimit-Remaining/RateLimit-Reset headers on a 429 -- confirmed live,
the limit is 100 requests/hour, reset on a fixed clock-hour boundary, and
NOT raised by OAuth authentication (despite this session's earlier
dryad_auth() work assuming it would be). The existing .storage_backoff()
only recognises the older Retry-After header, which Dryad never sends at
all, so every retry did blind exponential backoff (2s/4s/8s.../30s cap)
against a bucket that was provably empty until the next hour -- repeatedly
re-triggering the same wasted retry storm for every file in every affected
dataset, and very likely a major contributing factor to the heavy-429
conditions that preceded the crash.

The same header family (or the older X-RateLimit-* convention) is
confirmed live on Zenodo, GitHub, and GitLab too -- all four backends this
session has touched -- so this is built as shared logic across every
download call site, not a Dryad-specific patch. OSF/Figshare/Dataverse do
not expose it on the endpoints checked and are unaffected either way.

- .rate_limit_wait(): reads either header family off a 429 response,
  returns the real wait in seconds or NA if unconfirmed/absent.
- .storage_retry_after_factory() / .storage_is_transient_factory(): wired
  into req_retry()'s after/is_transient at every per-file download call
  site (.download_one(), .download_many_parallel()), so a
  confirmed-exhausted 429 waits for the REAL reset instead of blind
  backoff.
- .download_zip_to_cache() (the whole-dataset zip path) gains its own
  rate-limit check too: previously a 429's small error-page body would
  reach the streaming loop and either fail unzip() with a confusing
  "not a zip file" error or (worse) get silently treated as if it were
  real archive bytes. Now checks the status explicitly and waits for a
  confirmed reset (one retry) before falling through to the caller's
  file-by-file fallback.
- req_retry()'s own waits are completely silent by default -- a
  multi-minute-to-hour-long wait with zero console output looks identical
  to a hung process. A message() now announces any wait over 5 seconds,
  with the exact duration and how to skip it.
- New skip_on_api_limit parameter on download_repo_files() (default
  FALSE, i.e. always wait for the real reset -- explicit decision: the
  goal is completeness, not speed, for an unattended corpus build). TRUE
  gives up on a confirmed-exhausted request immediately instead, recorded
  in the failed attribute with an "API rate limit exhausted: "-prefixed
  message, filterable from every other kind of failure, so a caller can
  retry those specific files later once the quota has reset.

8 new unit tests in test-repo-download.R (1 skipped: an httr2
local_mocked_responses()/req_retry() interaction confirmed to behave
unreliably specifically under full-suite test ordering, not a bug in the
fix -- covered instead by an adjacent test using the more reliable
local_mocked_bindings() mock path; see that test's own comment). Full
package suite otherwise unaffected: FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 68 | PASS 4314.

recent_commits.message: release: v2.4.137 — a fix in the COMPARISON KEY is not a fix in the SHIPPED string
recent_commits.body:
v1.9.57 diagnosed that one stray U+0008 BACKSPACE made a Frontiers running
header unequal to its layout-channel twin, and fixed it inside `_key()` — F0's
comparison key. The character stayed in the emitted text, where a completely
unrelated rule landed on it one day later:
`_prior_paragraph_is_sentence_terminated` walks back over whitespace and
requires what it finds to be in ".!?/". On 10.3389/fvets.2025.1645266 the walk
landed on the BACKSPACE, discarded the `1 Introduction:` heading, and greedy
span-fill handed the preceding KEYWORDS span 69,849 characters — the whole
article. Found by an external benchmark, not by us.

* C0 `_strip_furniture_controls` (NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.58), run before F0
  so the comparison key and the output are ONE rule. One character wide and
  measured: all 33 corpus U+0008 sites are '.'+BS+newline, none are overstrike.
  U+0002/03/04/07 are corrupted CONTENT glyphs (Schri<02>macher =
  "Schrittmacher") and are COUNTED, not stripped, in the new
  `NormalizationReport.residual_control_chars`.
* The heading guard skips page breaks and control characters, and a canonical
  heading carrying BOTH a line-initial section number AND a colon no longer
  needs a terminated prior paragraph (SECTIONING_VERSION 1.2.5). Both halves
  are required: `2 Literature search` on the same paper resolves canonically to
  `references`, so a number-only escape would open back-matter mid-article.
  Measured blast radius: 3 of 39 guard rejections were furniture; the escape
  fires exactly once in 30 papers.
* The boundary-truncation pass, unreachable since v1.6.1 (`_NO_TRUNCATE =
  set(SectionLabel)` matched every label), is deleted.

The C0 strip ALONE does not fix that paper — the first probe said it did,
because it stripped the character from an already-normalized string while the
shipped order runs C0 before H0. Test the composition that ships (LESSONS
L-055, L-056).

Arena effect, 30 held-out PMC papers: body-label slice 0.7681 -> 0.7911,
oracle 0.8038 -> 0.8140, collapses 5 -> 4, recall median 0.9862, 0 regressions.

Gates: 2,885 passed / 0 failed; non-statistic corpus scan CLEAN 60/60;
render-deletion 26/26 with 0 content lost; verify_corpus 26/26 COVERAGE 26/26;
service suite 183 passed; public-repo hygiene 11/11.

code says why: they are runtime facts this repo does not define, so there is no
constant for them to drift from. Recording the reason matters more than the
exclusion -- an unexplained gap reads as an oversight to the next maintainer.

recent_commits.message: Wait for the real rate-limit reset instead of blind exponential backoff
recent_commits.body:
Found while investigating a code_check crash in a real 1861-paper corpus
run: Dryad's file-download endpoint sends IETF-draft RateLimit-Limit/
RateLimit-Remaining/RateLimit-Reset headers on a 429 -- confirmed live,
the limit is 100 requests/hour, reset on a fixed clock-hour boundary, and
NOT raised by OAuth authentication (despite this session's earlier
dryad_auth() work assuming it would be). The existing .storage_backoff()
only recognises the older Retry-After header, which Dryad never sends at
all, so every retry did blind exponential backoff (2s/4s/8s.../30s cap)
against a bucket that was provably empty until the next hour -- repeatedly
re-triggering the same wasted retry storm for every file in every affected
dataset, and very likely a major contributing factor to the heavy-429
conditions that preceded the crash.

The same header family (or the older X-RateLimit-* convention) is
confirmed live on Zenodo, GitHub, and GitLab too -- all four backends this
session has touched -- so this is built as shared logic across every
download call site, not a Dryad-specific patch. OSF/Figshare/Dataverse do
not expose it on the endpoints checked and are unaffected either way.

- .rate_limit_wait(): reads either header family off a 429 response,
  returns the real wait in seconds or NA if unconfirmed/absent.
- .storage_retry_after_factory() / .storage_is_transient_factory(): wired
  into req_retry()'s after/is_transient at every per-file download call
  site (.download_one(), .download_many_parallel()), so a
  confirmed-exhausted 429 waits for the REAL reset instead of blind
  backoff.
- .download_zip_to_cache() (the whole-dataset zip path) gains its own
  rate-limit check too: previously a 429's small error-page body would
  reach the streaming loop and either fail unzip() with a confusing
  "not a zip file" error or (worse) get silently treated as if it were
  real archive bytes. Now checks the status explicitly and waits for a
  confirmed reset (one retry) before falling through to the caller's
  file-by-file fallback.
- req_retry()'s own waits are completely silent by default -- a
  multi-minute-to-hour-long wait with zero console output looks identical
  to a hung process. A message() now announces any wait over 5 seconds,
  with the exact duration and how to skip it.
- New skip_on_api_limit parameter on download_repo_files() (default
  FALSE, i.e. always wait for the real reset -- explicit decision: the
  goal is completeness, not speed, for an unattended corpus build). TRUE
  gives up on a confirmed-exhausted request immediately instead, recorded
  in the failed attribute with an "API rate limit exhausted: "-prefixed
  message, filterable from every other kind of failure, so a caller can
  retry those specific files later once the quota has reset.

recent_commits.body: Support Figshare project URLs; surface unresolvable private share links
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Support Figshare project URLs; surface unresolvable private share links
recent_commits.body:
Found while checking metacheck's output against Cooper et al.'s corpus:
an interim comparison run on the first 250 papers found 6 where Cooper
coded a real Figshare-hosted dataset but metacheck detected no repository
at all. Traced to two unsupported Figshare URL shapes -- neither a general
Figshare failure, since plain article/DOI links already worked correctly.

1. Project URLs (figshare.com/projects/<name>/<id>)

   A project bundles multiple articles rather than being one, so it has
   no article id of its own -- .figshare_id() correctly returned NA for
   it, but nothing then tried to resolve it as a project. Added
   .figshare_project_id() (extracts the trailing numeric id) and
   .figshare_project_articles() (lists the project's article ids via the
   public, unauthenticated GET /v2/projects/{id}/articles endpoint),
   wired into figshare_info() so a project url expands into one row per
   article -- the same shape as if the paper had cited each article url
   directly. Verified live against a real project (PERICLES Heritage
   values, 8 articles): repo_check() on the affected paper now finds 94
   files, up from 0.

   Also extended figshare_links()'s bare-text regex to match /projects/
   urls at all (it previously only matched articles/ndownloader), since
   both of the two real project-url misses in the sample were bare text
   mentions rather than real hyperlinks.

2. Private share links (figshare.com/s/<hash>)

   The hash is an opaque token with no article id anywhere in the URL,
   and Figshare's own resolution page sits behind an AWS WAF bot
   challenge -- confirmed live: a plain request gets an explicit "we
   need to verify you're not a robot... this requires JavaScript"
   challenge page, on every URL variant tried (the bare share link, one
   with a file= query parameter, and the direct ndownloader endpoint
   with a private_link= parameter, all three revealed by following a
   real browser's redirect chain). No documented plain-HTTP API
   alternative exists for a third party to resolve someone else's share
   link (the /v2/account/articles/{id}/private_links/ family is for the
   owner managing their own links). Passing the challenge programmatically
   would require emulating a real browser session, which is out of scope
   as bot-detection evasion.

   Rather than staying invisible (previously indistinguishable from "no
   Figshare link found"), figshare_links() now flags these via a new
   figshare_unsupported column, and repo_check() surfaces them through
   repo_error ("private share link cannot be resolved without a
   browser") -- the same mechanism already used for a private OSF
   project or a gated repository, so the link is visible in gated_repos
   for a human to follow up on manually.

Added tests/testthat/test-archive-figshare.R (28 assertions), since
Figshare previously had no dedicated test file at all.

recent_commits.message: Fix Dryad whole-dataset zip download and add a real byte-cap during zip streaming
recent_commits.body:
download_repo_files() already had a Dryad zip-download branch (using the
stash:download bulk endpoint) that was supposed to replace N per-file
requests with one archive request, but it was silently dead code for the
entire Cooper corpus: the eligibility check matched repo_url against
"datadryad.org" only, while every real repo_url in the corpus is the
doi.org citation form (e.g. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.8sf7m0cjc) --
file_url (the per-file link) is datadryad.org, but repo_url never is. Every
Dryad dataset therefore fell through to file-by-file downloads (2 + N
requests each), which is what was driving the HTTP 429s seen at corpus
scale, independent of authentication.

Fixes, all verified live against real Dryad datasets from the corpus:

- Zip-eligibility regex now also matches the doi.org/10.5061/dryad form.
- .remote_content_length() gains a req_func parameter so its HEAD probe can
  be authenticated -- needed because Dryad requires a token for ANY call
  touching file bytes, including HEAD, unlike every other backend this
  function probes.
- Dryad's bulk endpoint still can't report its size via either method (HEAD
  answers 403 InvalidSignatureException -- its pre-signed S3 URL's
  signature is verb-specific; GET is chunked with no Content-Length at
  all), so the zip-vs-file-by-file size gate now falls back to summing the
  file sizes repo_check() already listed as a conservative estimate,
  rather than always failing "unknown size" and disabling the zip path
  permanently for this backend.
- .download_zip_to_cache() rewritten to stream via req_perform_connection()
  (req_perform_stream() is deprecated as of httr2 1.2.0) with a real
  max_bytes cap enforced DURING the download and a manual wall-clock
  timeout to replace the one req_timeout() no longer provides in this mode.
  Wired max_download_size through to it for OSF/Zenodo/Dataverse/Dryad
  (not GitHub/GitLab, whose zip transport is deliberately unbounded by
  design). This closes metacheck issue #366's second bug: a zip fallback
  with only a wall-clock timeout can still pull many GB on a fast
  connection before timing out (the issue's own example: 2.47GB for one
  failed text file on OSF).

Verified end-to-end against doi:10.5061/dryad.8sf7m0cjc: the fix correctly
downloads all 3 files as one zip request instead of 3+2, and a deliberately
tiny max_bytes correctly aborts the stream with zero files extracted.

recent_commits.body: Add GitLab support and surface repository licence/DOI metadata
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Add GitLab support and surface repository licence/DOI metadata
recent_commits.body:
Adds a full GitLab.com backend (archive-gitlab.R), matching the shape of
the existing GitHub backend: link detection (gitlab.com URLs and bare
"owner/repo" mentions near "gitlab"), repo path parsing, a paginated
file-tree listing (GitLab's tree endpoint caps at 100 entries/page, unlike
GitHub's single-request Git Trees API), file-size backfill via a batched
GraphQL repository.blobs(paths:) query (the REST tree listing has no size
field), licence detection, and complete-repository download via GitLab's
archive.zip endpoint (wired into repo-download.R the same way GitHub's
zipball is, since neither supports HTTP Range requests for a zip_peek()-
style partial read).

Separately, surfaces doi/license metadata in repo_check()'s new
repo_metadata field (one row per repository, not per paper -- a paper can
link more than one repository with different licences) for every backend
that already fetches this as part of a request it makes anyway: Dryad,
Zenodo, Dataverse, Figshare, ReShare, GitHub, GitLab, and PsychArchives
(the last via a new "doi" attribute on psycharchives_file_download(),
alongside its existing "rights" attribute). Previously this data was
fetched and then discarded before reaching the module's output. OSF's
licence is included too, but gated behind a new osf_license parameter
(default FALSE) since OSF requires one genuinely additional API request
per project that this module would not otherwise make, unlike every other
backend above.

Four real bugs were found and fixed while verifying this against live
GitLab.com repositories:
- New GitLab functions were tagged @export but NAMESPACE was never
  regenerated, so none of them were actually callable.
- httr2::req_url_query() silently breaks (404) when the request path
  already contains a percent-encoded segment (GitLab's "namespace%2Fproject"
  project id) -- fixed by building query strings directly into the URL.
- c() on a named list of named vectors prefixes each inner name with the
  outer list's name ("1..dockerignore" instead of ".dockerignore"),
  silently corrupting the path->size lookup in .gitlab_blob_sizes() even
  though the underlying GraphQL data was correct -- fixed with unname().
- GitLab's GraphQL API enforces a query-complexity budget (default max
  200); a blobs(paths:) query with 100 paths costs 212 and fails outright
  (HTTP 200 with an error in the body, not an HTTP error status, so this
  failed silently). Empirically confirmed the real cutoff is 94 paths;
  batch size reduced from 100 to 90 for margin.

Verified live against gitlab-org/gitlab-runner (1432 files, full
pagination, all files with backfilled sizes, licence "mit" correctly
detected) and end-to-end through repo_check() (table/summary_table/
repo_metadata all correctly populated). Cross-checked that Dryad's
repo_metadata (real doi + CC0 licence) and other existing backends are
unaffected.

recent_commits.message: Add Dryad OAuth2 client-credentials auth (resolves #370)
recent_commits.body:
dryad_pat() only accepts a single, manually-obtained OAuth2 bearer token,
which Dryad issues with a 10-hour lifetime. Any corpus run longer than 10
hours (or any interactive session spanning a coffee break) needed the
token manually regenerated and re-set mid-run, since .dryad_headers()
just attached whatever static string dryad_pat() currently held.

Dryad also issues a client id/secret pair, meant for the OAuth2
client-credentials grant (POST https://datadryad.org/oauth/token) --
trading those credentials for a short-lived access token that gets
refreshed automatically for as long as the credentials stay valid, with
no manual re-entry.

Adds dryad_auth(client_id, client_secret), parallel to dryad_pat(), that
stores the credentials (also readable from DRYAD_CLIENT_ID/
DRYAD_CLIENT_SECRET environment variables, the same way dryad_pat() reads
DRYAD_PAT) and builds an httr2::oauth_client(). .dryad_headers() now uses
httr2::req_oauth_client_credentials() when a client is set -- which
handles the whole token fetch/cache/automatic-refresh cycle transparently
-- falling back to the existing static dryad_pat() bearer header when
only a raw token is available.

Verified live: dryad_auth() correctly read real client credentials from
the environment, and dryad_file_download() against a real Dryad dataset
downloaded all 3 files successfully with checksums verified, confirming
the token exchange works end-to-end for actual file downloads (not just
metadata/listing calls, which never required a token).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Attach paper_id to naming_issues; fix empty-result schema loss on batch runs
recent_commits.body:
Two related follow-ups to the per-paper summary_table fix (d53090b),
both found while testing a batched multi-paper corpus run:

repo_check: the module's returned naming_issues field was still the
corpus-wide, unattributed table (keyed only by file_name), not the
paper_id-tagged version already built for the per-paper summary_table
count. data_check() reads this field via get_prev_outputs("repo_check",
"naming_issues") for its own per-file "Naming issue" column, so on a
multi-paper run it could not tell which paper a naming issue belonged to.
Fixed by returning the already-built, paper_id-tagged table instead of
the untagged one. Also fixed a related bug this surfaced in
codebook_check.R: its empty-result path computed a fallback paper_id set
from unique(structure_df$paper_id), which breaks when structure_df is a
real but zero-row data frame (character(0), not "no such column") --
this now falls through to .pid() correctly in that case too, instead of
producing a data.frame() row-count mismatch error.

code_check/codebook_check/data_check: each has an early-return path for
"nothing found" (no relevant code files; no extracted data columns; no
files at all) that returned either no `table` field at all or a bare,
schema-less data.frame(). Confirmed on a real 2-paper test batch where
neither paper had any code file: code_check's table came back with ZERO
columns instead of the normal paper_id/file_location/language/... schema.
On a corpus or batch run, even one paper hitting this path could silently
drop columns (or fill them with NA) for every other paper once combined
with bind_rows(). Each now returns its already-available, correctly-typed
but zero-row base frame instead.

Verified against test-module-repo_check.R, test-module-codebook_check.R,
and test-codebook-helpers.R (all pass), plus live reproductions of both
original bugs on real papers.

recent_commits.message: release: v2.4.137 — a fix in the COMPARISON KEY is not a fix in the SHIPPED string
recent_commits.body:
v1.9.57 diagnosed that one stray U+0008 BACKSPACE made a Frontiers running
header unequal to its layout-channel twin, and fixed it inside `_key()` — F0's
comparison key. The character stayed in the emitted text, where a completely
unrelated rule landed on it one day later:
`_prior_paragraph_is_sentence_terminated` walks back over whitespace and
requires what it finds to be in ".!?/". On 10.3389/fvets.2025.1645266 the walk
landed on the BACKSPACE, discarded the `1 Introduction:` heading, and greedy
span-fill handed the preceding KEYWORDS span 69,849 characters — the whole
article. Found by an external benchmark, not by us.

* C0 `_strip_furniture_controls` (NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.58), run before F0
  so the comparison key and the output are ONE rule. One character wide and
  measured: all 33 corpus U+0008 sites are '.'+BS+newline, none are overstrike.
  U+0002/03/04/07 are corrupted CONTENT glyphs (Schri<02>macher =
  "Schrittmacher") and are COUNTED, not stripped, in the new
  `NormalizationReport.residual_control_chars`.
* The heading guard skips page breaks and control characters, and a canonical
  heading carrying BOTH a line-initial section number AND a colon no longer
  needs a terminated prior paragraph (SECTIONING_VERSION 1.2.5). Both halves
  are required: `2 Literature search` on the same paper resolves canonically to
  `references`, so a number-only escape would open back-matter mid-article.
  Measured blast radius: 3 of 39 guard rejections were furniture; the escape
  fires exactly once in 30 papers.
* The boundary-truncation pass, unreachable since v1.6.1 (`_NO_TRUNCATE =
  set(SectionLabel)` matched every label), is deleted.

The C0 strip ALONE does not fix that paper — the first probe said it did,
because it stripped the character from an already-normalized string while the
shipped order runs C0 before H0. Test the composition that ships (LESSONS
L-055, L-056).

Arena effect, 30 held-out PMC papers: body-label slice 0.7681 -> 0.7911,
oracle 0.8038 -> 0.8140, collapses 5 -> 4, recall median 0.9862, 0 regressions.

Gates: 2,885 passed / 0 failed; non-statistic corpus scan CLEAN 60/60;
render-deletion 26/26 with 0 content lost; verify_corpus 26/26 COVERAGE 26/26;
service suite 183 passed; public-repo hygiene 11/11.

recent_commits.message: docs(changelog): v2.4.136's measurements were the LAYOUT path, presented as universal
recent_commits.body:
The entry said "16 papers gain page breaks; 2 footnote appendices restored" with
no indication of which callers see it. Two of those three claims do not reach the
HTTP API at all, and the entry as written told consumers otherwise.

`_f0_strip_running_and_footnotes` returns immediately without a `LayoutDoc`, and
the footnote appendix is F0's product. Enumerated rather than assumed:

    batch.py:355              passes layout   -> full change
    sections/__init__.py:116  passes layout   -> full change
    service/app/main.py:532   NO layout       -> page breaks only
    service/app/main.py:1007  NO layout       -> page breaks only

Re-measured through the no-layout path the service actually runs: 12 of 26 papers
change (not 16), 0 appendices restored (not 2), and still 0 lines removed or
added. The API gains page boundaries and loses nothing; it gains no appendix.

AND THE LARGER FINDING, pre-existing and not this release's doing: because the
service never computes a layout, F0 has NEVER run in production, and neither has
any layout-gated repair -- W0h (dropped minus via cid glyph), W0m (beta-as-b via
font), W0p (superscript via size+baseline). Every API consumer has been receiving
text with running headers intact and those three repairs absent, while the same
document through `extract_to_dir` is repaired. Two paths, one version, different
numbers.

This is the identical shape CLAUDE.md records for batch.py and marks FIXED in
v2.4.128 -- the service was never checked. NOT fixed here: wiring a layout into
the service roughly doubles per-document cost and changes output for every
consumer at once, which is a deliberate decision, not a doc fix. Tracked in the
handoff and in both consumer notices.

Bumps __version__ + pyproject to 2.4.136 and promotes the CHANGELOG entry.
NORMALIZATION_VERSION was already at 1.9.57 (cd89380), because the output
changed then and the version describing that output had to move with it.

recent_commits.message: test(gate): the docs-accuracy gate had no test, and was edited twice in one session
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/check_docs_consistency.py` asserts that the version numbers
`docs/README.md` advertises still match the constants this package defines. It is
invoked by hand from handoffs and release checklists and by nothing automatic —
so it was changed twice today (2657047, ab291c7) with nothing pinning either
change, and the second of those changes existed only because the first had a gap
nobody could have caught.

A check that CAN be a test MUST be a test. A gate nobody runs is
indistinguishable from a gate that passes, and this one guards a claim that
reaches consumers: `docs/README.md` documents the provenance block
`get_version_info()` returns.

Five cases, each pinning a failure that actually happened or is about to:

  * the gate PASSES on the committed tree
  * a drifted PACKAGE version is caught — the one that goes stale on EVERY
    release, uncovered until ab291c7
  * a drifted PIPELINE version is caught — `table_extraction_version` sat at
    '2.4.10' against a source 2.4.12 until it was spotted by eye
  * a drifted NORMALIZATION version is caught
  * the two deliberately-ungated keys are still NAMED in the gate, so the reason
    for excluding them cannot be silently lost

Each drift runs against a COPY of only the files the gate reads, in tmp — the
test never mutates the working tree, and does not drag the corpus along.

MUTATION-VERIFIED IN TWO DIRECTIONS, because a test that has never failed against
the real defect proves nothing:

  removing the package-version line   -> exactly 1 test fails
  removing the whole sibling loop     -> 3 tests fail

recent_commits.message: fix(gate): the version check missed the ONE version that goes stale every release
recent_commits.body:
Hard rule 23 says a universal-quantifier claim is only as good as the enumeration
behind it. The previous commit's message claimed the gate "compares every
advertised pipeline version against its defining constant". Enumerating the
provenance block in docs/README.md rather than trusting that sentence:

    advertised   version, normalize_version, sectioning_version,
                 table_extraction_version, python_version, unicodedata_version
    covered      normalize_version, sectioning_version, table_extraction_version
    UNCOVERED    version, python_version, unicodedata_version

Six keys, not the five I had in mind -- `unicodedata_version` was not even on my
list. The claim was defensible for the three PIPELINE versions and silent about
the rest, which is exactly the shape rule 23 exists to catch.

`version` is now covered, and it is the important one: it is the package version,
so it goes stale on EVERY release, and docs/README.md advertises it as `2.4.135`.
The very next release would have made that doc wrong with nothing to say so.

`python_version` and `unicodedata_version` are deliberately NOT gated, and the
code says why: they are runtime facts this repo does not define, so there is no
constant for them to drift from. Recording the reason matters more than the
exclusion -- an unexplained gap reads as an oversight to the next maintainer.

Mutation-verified: setting __version__ = 2.4.136 fails with
"docs/README.md says version = '2.4.135' but docpluck/__init__.py defines
__version__ = '2.4.136'", and restoring it passes.

recent_commits.message: Support Figshare project URLs; surface unresolvable private share links
recent_commits.body:
Found while checking metacheck's output against Cooper et al.'s corpus:
an interim comparison run on the first 250 papers found 6 where Cooper
coded a real Figshare-hosted dataset but metacheck detected no repository
at all. Traced to two unsupported Figshare URL shapes -- neither a general
Figshare failure, since plain article/DOI links already worked correctly.

1. Project URLs (figshare.com/projects/<name>/<id>)

   A project bundles multiple articles rather than being one, so it has
   no article id of its own -- .figshare_id() correctly returned NA for
   it, but nothing then tried to resolve it as a project. Added
   .figshare_project_id() (extracts the trailing numeric id) and
   .figshare_project_articles() (lists the project's article ids via the
   public, unauthenticated GET /v2/projects/{id}/articles endpoint),
   wired into figshare_info() so a project url expands into one row per
   article -- the same shape as if the paper had cited each article url
   directly. Verified live against a real project (PERICLES Heritage
   values, 8 articles): repo_check() on the affected paper now finds 94
   files, up from 0.

   Also extended figshare_links()'s bare-text regex to match /projects/
   urls at all (it previously only matched articles/ndownloader), since
   both of the two real project-url misses in the sample were bare text
   mentions rather than real hyperlinks.

2. Private share links (figshare.com/s/<hash>)

   The hash is an opaque token with no article id anywhere in the URL,
   and Figshare's own resolution page sits behind an AWS WAF bot
   challenge -- confirmed live: a plain request gets an explicit "we
   need to verify you're not a robot... this requires JavaScript"
   challenge page, on every URL variant tried (the bare share link, one
   with a file= query parameter, and the direct ndownloader endpoint
   with a private_link= parameter, all three revealed by following a
   real browser's redirect chain). No documented plain-HTTP API
   alternative exists for a third party to resolve someone else's share
   link (the /v2/account/articles/{id}/private_links/ family is for the
   owner managing their own links). Passing the challenge programmatically
   would require emulating a real browser session, which is out of scope
   as bot-detection evasion.

   Rather than staying invisible (previously indistinguishable from "no
   Figshare link found"), figshare_links() now flags these via a new
   figshare_unsupported column, and repo_check() surfaces them through
   repo_error ("private share link cannot be resolved without a
   browser") -- the same mechanism already used for a private OSF
   project or a gated repository, so the link is visible in gated_repos
   for a human to follow up on manually.

Added tests/testthat/test-archive-figshare.R (28 assertions), since
Figshare previously had no dedicated test file at all.
